lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The quake. The waves. A long night on the hill.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Morning came cold and gray. Nobody had really slept.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: Good news. I'm still waterproof.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Bad news. Nothing else is.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Below them, Gull Harbor was gone.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: Mags... the ferry's on Main Street.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: So is half the harbor.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: Someone'll come, right? Helicopters? Coast Guard?

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Look at the bridge.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: No boats. No helicopters. No one on the road.

lines.speaker: NEIGHBOR_F
lines.text: It's been a whole night. Where is everybody?

lines.speaker: NEIGHBOR
lines.text: They'll come. They have to.

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: Folks! Listen up! Help is on its way.

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: Till then, we stay calm and organized.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: He doesn't know that. Nobody does.

lines.speaker: RADIO
lines.text: ...the entire coast, Oregon to British Columbia...

lines.speaker: RADIO
lines.text: ...roads and bridges impassable... Highway one-oh-one...

lines.speaker: RADIO
lines.text: ...relief may take days... possibly weeks...

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: ...Weeks?

lines.speaker: NEIGHBOR_F
lines.text: Weeks?! We'll be dead in weeks!

lines.speaker: NEIGHBOR
lines.text: I'm driving out. I'm not waiting.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Drive where? There's no road left.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Fear spreads fast when there's nothing to do.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: Okay. Then let's do something.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Don't drink that!

lines.speaker: NEIGHBOR
lines.text: It's just rainwater.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: It's runoff. Sewage, fuel, chemicals.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: What about the cabin tap?

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Pipes broke. Catch rain clean, then boil it.

lines.speaker: NEIGHBOR
lines.text: My boy's freezing. Just for a few minutes.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: Mags— the stove!

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Not in there. Not ever.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Carbon monoxide. You can't see it or smell it.

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: Okay. Everything you brought — on the table.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Most people had run with nothing but their phones.

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: Three waters. Chips. A lighter. That's it?

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: I've got... a granola bar to add!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Everyone saw what else was in the bag.

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: Well, well. What've you got there, Drizzle?

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: One pile. I ration it. Fair for everyone.

lines.speaker: NEIGHBOR
lines.text: Yeah! Why should he keep it?

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: I want to help, but who decides who gets what?

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: I do. Somebody has to.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Nobody takes anything from anybody. Not today.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Yesterday they were neighbors. Today they were counting.

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: You too, Tess. What's in the bag?

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: Mine. For my son.

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: There's no 'mine' anymore. Not up here.

lines.speaker: TESS
lines.text: Says the man holding the list.

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: We'll talk later. Everybody shares.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: She looks like I feel.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Ration the food from day one.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: And the water?

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Drink what you need. Then find more.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: And keep that bag out of sight. People notice.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: Shh. Our secret. Eat it slow.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Every house up here has a hidden water tank.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: The water heater? That's forty gallons!

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Power off. Close the intake, or bad water gets in.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Open a hot tap, then the drain.

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: Listen up! Dale's store has a whole pallet of water!

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: Four of us. In and out before lunch.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Into the flood zone? Any aftershock can send another wave.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Lines down. Gas leaking. Walls cracked.

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: People are thirsty. I won't wait weeks.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Dale's Gas and Grocery. The flood zone.

lines.speaker: PRUITT
lines.text: Gord... you smell that?

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: Just grab the water. Fast.

lines.speaker: PRUITT
lines.text: Watch the wire! Stay out of that puddle!

lines.speaker: GORD
lines.text: Pallet's right inside. Get the door open.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: Water first. Stoves outside. Ration. Stay out of the flood zone.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Tell that to Gord.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Dale's Gas & Grocery went up in black smoke.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: No. No, no, no—

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Stay here. Nobody else goes down. Nobody.

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: First-aid kit. They'll need it—

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: ...Where's my bag?

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: It was right here. Right HERE.

lines.speaker: MAGS
lines.text: Who knew where you kept it?

lines.speaker: DRIZZLE
lines.text: ...Everyone saw it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Smoke below. An empty spot. No one coming.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Next... Day one. Night.
